Strict version, validating month and day ranges (it doesn't check days-per-month, so `2026-02-31` still matches):

```
\b\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])\b
```

Simpler version, if you only need the shape:

```
\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}
```

If you need the whole string to be a date, anchor it instead of using `\b`:

```
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

`2026-10-01` matches all three. For real calendar validation (leap years, 30-day months), parse the string with a date library after the regex check.
